# LiveTradeBench: Seeking Real-World Alpha with Large Language Models

arXiv [2511.03628](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03628) · v1 2025-11-05 · latest 2025-11-05

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | A live trading benchmark evaluating LLM agents on multi-asset portfolio allocation in real-time U.S. stock and Polymarket prediction markets. | “To address this, we introduce LiveTradeBench, a live trading environment for evaluating LLM agents in realistic and evolving markets.” |
| **architecture** | ReAct-style single agent with tool use (feature extraction from prices/news), fixed-horizon memory of past observations, and reasoning; outputs JSON allocation vectors summing to 1 including cash, long-only. | “To provide a controlled yet extensible setup, we adopt a React-style (Yao et al., 2022) framework equipped with tool use and memory as our agent configuration.” |
| **data** | 15 U.S. equities (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, META, JPM, V, XOM, CAT, TSLA, PG, KO, AMZN, WMT, JNJ, UNH) plus cash via yfinance daily bars; 10 Polymarket binary markets via CLOB endpoints; news from Google News (and Reddit). | “Prices come from a public finance API (equities) and Polymarket CLOB endpoints (prediction markets); context comes from Google News and Reddit.” |
| **window** | Live evaluation from August 18, 2025 to October 24, 2025, 50 trading days; no training split. | “live trading conducted from August 18, 2025, to October 24, 2025—a total of 50 trading days—across trading agents built on 21 unique LLM backbones.” |
| **models** | 21 LLMs: GPT-5, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-o3; Claude-Opus-4.1, Opus-4, Sonnet-4, Sonnet-3.7; Gemini-2.5-Pro/Flash; Grok-4/3; Llama4-Maverick/Scout, Llama3.3-70B; Qwen3-235B-A22B Instruct/Thinking, Qwen2.5-72B; DeepSeek-R1/V3.1; Kimi-K2-Instruct. Temperature 0.3. | “\| OpenAI \| GPT-5, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-o3” |
| **baselines** | *not found in the text provided* | |
| **headline_result** | GPT-4.1 achieved the highest stock cumulative return 6.25% (Sharpe 2.64) over the 50 days, but -33.69% on Polymarket; LMArena-vs-return Spearman correlation 0.054 (stocks) and -0.38 (Polymarket). | “\| GPT-4.1 \| 6.25 \| 2.64 \| 1.92 \| 65.31 \| 10.51 \| -33.69 \| -1.74 \| 37.98 \| 40.82 \| 95.27” |
| **costs** | No transaction fees, bid-ask spreads, liquidity constraints or other frictions are modeled. | “Our current environment and evaluation do not account for transaction fees, bid–ask spreads, liquidity constraints, or other real-world trading frictions.” |
| **uncertainty** | Single live run per model; rolling-k delta analysis reports mean across 21 models with 25–75% band. No seeds or significance tests reported. | “The black line denotes the mean performance across 21 models, and the shaded gray region indicates the 25–75% confidence interval.” |
| **leakage_controls** | Live streaming evaluation avoids backtest leakage; news queried over [t-3, t-1] and price history uses 10-day lookback ending at t-1 to reduce same-day leakage. | “For a trading day t , we query Google News over a short window [t{-}3,t{-}1] to reduce same-day leakage while preserving timeliness.” |
| **limitations** | No transaction costs/frictions; limited observation and action spaces due to context length (few markets, truncated news); simplified ReAct agent design without multi-agent or RL. | “Ignoring these factors may overestimate achievable returns, especially for strategies that rely on frequent rebalancing.” |
| **release** | Open-source Python package live-trade-bench on PyPI, GitHub repo github.com/ulab-uiuc/live-trade-bench, and live web app trade-bench.live. | “To democratize research on LLM-based trading agents, we release an open-source Python package, live-trade-bench22 2 https://pypi.org/project/live-trade-bench/ , which provides simple APIs for data collection, environment setup, and agent construction.” |
